answers.question: What do we know about fire at 34 percent oxygen?

segments.text: Counting every test at or above 30% oxygen at any pressure gives 507 tests: 483 gas flame tests, 24 droplet tests and 0 solid material tests
In FLEX, flames went out in only 2 of 24 droplet tests at 28 to 36% oxygen, and the median extinction ratio was 0.23 in that band
PSI holds no solid material tests at or above 30% oxygen, while the highest oxygen level in any solid material test is 22.2%
The solid material tests in BASS-II covered 13.6% to 22.2% oxygen and so do not reach 34%
The Exploration atmosphere has an Evidence Coverage of 67 out of 100

answers.question: Which investigations tested fabrics?

segments.text: BASS (PSI-26) burned cotton and fiberglass fabric (SIBAL) among its solid samples
Saffire-I (PSI-98) burned a large sheet of cotton and fiberglass fabric inside an uncrewed Cygnus cargo vehicle
Saffire-II (PSI-99) tested cotton and fiberglass fabric alongside silicone, PMMA and Nomex samples
Saffire-III (PSI-100) burned a large sheet of cotton and fiberglass fabric at a higher air flow than Saffire-I
BASS-II (PSI-25) tested cotton and fiberglass fabric (SIBAL) samples as well

answers.question: How was carbon dioxide tested as a suppressant?

segments.text: The FLEX investigation (PSI-69) burned single droplets of methanol and heptane in microgravity and varied the oxygen level, pressure, and added gases carbon dioxide and helium
Carbon dioxide was tested as a gaseous suppressant by burning droplets in atmospheres with it added, to see how well it put out the flame
Carbon dioxide works as a diluent, an inert gas that takes heat from a flame and can extinguish it

answers.question: What is a cool flame?

segments.text: A cool flame is a flame that burns at a low temperature with little or no visible light
NASA's Researcher's Guide describes stable cool flames that form after the visible flame of a heptane droplet goes out
The CFI investigation studies cool flames, where a droplet keeps burning at low temperature after the visible flame goes out

answers.question: What is missing for the Moon?

segments.text: The PSI evidence shows that no combustion investigation has run at Moon or Mars gravity, with all 24 being microgravity or ground studies
Solid material tests stop at 22.2% oxygen, while a Moon Base is planned at 30% or more, and PSI holds 0 solid material tests at or above 30% oxygen
The planned LUCI and FM2 experiments are named as possible ways to close this oxygen gap
The Saffire-II results point to shorter burns in microgravity, but they come from 9 samples at one flow speed and about 22% oxygen, so they bound the question without settling it
The ACME E-FIELD Flames experiment used an electric field to mimic partial gravity, but its table states no oxygen value

answers.question: Which experiments shared hardware?

segments.text: Six ACME experiments shared the Combustion Integrated Rack hardware with the ACME insert, which burns gaseous fuels on the ISS
Those six were ACME Flame Design (PSI-10), ACME BRE (PSI-20), ACME CLD Flame (PSI-21), ACME E-FIELD Flames (PSI-22), ACME s-Flame (PSI-23) and ACME CFI-G (PSI-159)
The Combustion Integrated Rack with the Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus was shared by three investigations, CFI (PSI-39), FLEX-2 (PSI-68) and FLEX (PSI-69), which burn liquid fuel droplets
